content.text:
I found two codes in the knowledge store that show a person has hidradenitis suppurativa:

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| M25y1 | Hidradenitis |
| M25y1-1 | Hidradenitis suppurativa |

**What I left out:**
- **Similar-sounding conditions that aren't hidradenitis suppurativa:** hidradenoma (a sweat gland tumour, BB610-1, B76-8), Fox-Fordyce disease (M25y0), acne conglobata (M2611) and folliculitis abscedens et suffodiens (M2440). The last two often occur alongside hidradenitis suppurativa, but having one of them doesn't mean the person has it.
- **Wider categories:** boils, abscesses or cellulitis of the armpit or groin, and general sweat gland disorder codes such as M25y and Myu6J. These would wrongly pick up people who don't have the condition.
- **Surgery codes:** removal of sweat-gland-bearing skin from the armpit, groin or perineum (7G030, 7G031, 7G032, 7D076, 7C160). This surgery is a common treatment, but these codes record a procedure, not a diagnosis. You could add them as a separate list if you want to find people treated for it.

I also searched for other names and descriptions of the condition ("acne inversa", "Verneuil's disease", "apocrinitis", and hidradenitis of the armpit or groin). None of them found any more codes.

content.text:
I found two matching codes in the knowledge store:

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| M25y1 | Hidradenitis |
| M25y1-1 | Hidradenitis suppurativa |

**Why both are included:** M25y1-1 names the condition directly. M25y1 ("Hidradenitis") is the parent code above it. In this coding system, hidradenitis is generally recorded as hidradenitis suppurativa, so the parent code points to the same condition. If you want only codes that name the condition exactly, you could keep M25y1-1 alone, but you would probably miss some cases.

**Codes left out on purpose:**
- **Hidradenomas, hidrocystomas and sweat gland adenomas or adenocarcinomas** (e.g. B76-8, BB610-1, BB65): these are tumours, not this inflammatory disease.
- **Boils, carbuncles, abscesses and cellulitis of the armpit, groin or buttock** (e.g. M0131, M0031, M0940): these happen in the same places but aren't specific to hidradenitis suppurativa.
- **Acne conglobata (M2611), folliculitis abscedens et suffodiens (M2440) and pilonidal disease (M06)**: these are related conditions that often occur alongside it, but they are separate diagnoses.
- **Surgery to remove sweat gland-bearing skin** (e.g. 7G030, 7G031, 7G03E): this is a common treatment, but it records a procedure rather than a diagnosis, and it is also done for other conditions like heavy sweating.
- **Broad sweat gland disorder codes** (e.g. M25y, M25yX, Myu6D, Myu6J): too general.

content.text:
I searched the knowledge store with several terms: "hidradenitis suppurativa", "hidradenitis", "acne inversa", "apocrinitis", "hidradenitis axillaris", the ICD-10 code L73.2, and phrasing about the armpit and groin. Only two codes describe hidradenitis.

**Codelist: Hidradenitis suppurativa**

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| M25y1 | Hidradenitis |
| M25y1-1 | Hidradenitis suppurativa |

**Left out on purpose:**
- **Hidradenomas** (B76-8, BB610-1, BB610-2, BB63-1): these are sweat gland tumours, not hidradenitis.
- **Look-alike or related conditions:** acne conglobata (M2611), folliculitis abscedens et suffodiens (M2440), pilonidal disease (M06 and its child codes), Fox-Fordyce disease (M25y0) and pyoderma gangrenosum (M0702). They are clinically related but are separate diagnoses.
- **Boils, carbuncles and abscesses** of the armpit, groin, buttock or perineum (e.g. M0131, M0940, M0326). These often show up in people with the condition but don't confirm it, and including them would wrongly pick up many people without it.
- **Sweat gland excision procedures** (7G030, 7G031, 7G03E): these are used to treat the condition but aren't specific to it, so on their own they don't show a current diagnosis.
- **Broad parent and catch-all codes** (M25y, Myu6J, M25yX, Myu6D): too general to point to this condition.

M25y1 "Hidradenitis" is the parent of the suppurativa code and is kept in. It may occasionally pick up other forms of hidradenitis, but in practice it is used almost only for this condition.
